title: Motion blur on titles that move fast
goal: Anything in a title that moves fast (a word sliding in, a pill popping, a line wiping) can carry motion blur, the way professional titles do, so quick moves look smooth and filmic instead of stepping.
notes: User's words (2026-10-10): "the comps in the library for titles are so very bland. They look like powerpoint titles. I am wondering if we can have more professionally polished animated title screens with interesting, tweakable effects. Moving backgrounds, text that comes in, looks polished and designed, maybe motion blur, not like a template. do research on what good looking intros look like and derive how to make it easy to build these." The research and the model are in docs/design/video-titles-polish.md (READ IT FIRST: techniques, twelve style recipes, the TitleDesign/TitlePart/behaviour model that compiles to keys, renderer costs, today's gaps with file refs). Six tasks build it in order: titles-move-in-parts, title-text-by-line-word-letter, title-backgrounds-move, motion-blur-on-titles, title-tiles-play-and-knobs, a-set-of-titles-that-look-designed. This is step 4 of 6.
acceptance: A Motion Blur switch and a Shutter angle (default 180, up to 360) per layer and on a title as a whole, as non-destructive styling
Blur follows each moving part's own velocity (position, scale, rotation), and is drawn only while the part is moving faster than a small threshold, so held frames stay sharp

Start with a directional blur along the per-frame velocity; MEASURE frame cost at 1080p for a word stagger and a full-frame slide, and only add sub-frame sampling if the directional blur looks wrong in the photographed frames; perf note in the commit
Playback, scrubbing and export match; a held title is pixel identical with motion blur on and off
A walk plays a fast slide in with and without motion blur and photographs the same frame of each
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.
